title: Milan: incline intervals are back on, 5 x 5min at 10-12%
terrain: treadmill 10-12% incline, climbing only, zero descent

steps.target: Z1-Z2, 99-151 bpm, longer than usual if run in the morning

coachNotes:
EXECUTION: gradient fixed at 10-12%, drop belt speed if HR goes over 169. Walk the belt if 12% demands it, power-hiking trains the same system. 2min flat walking between reps, do not jog them. Rep 5 should look like rep 1. The 20min warmup is non-negotiable in the morning.
GYM AFTER (this is the actual ITBS work): side-lying hip abduction 3x15/side, clamshells 3x15/side, single-leg glute bridge 3x12/side, side plank with top-leg abduction 3x30s/side, Copenhagen plank 3x20s/side, single-leg calf raise 3x15. No step-downs, split squats or lunges this week.
FUEL: 1 Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro at minute 30 with 200ml water.
STOP RULE: a session passes only with no symptoms during, immediately after, and next day. Over 2/10 during the run, stop. Any fail drops the next session to the last level that passed.
WHY UPHILL: steep climbing keeps the knee out of the 20-30 degree compression band and has no braking phase, so it buys race-specific intensity at near-zero cost to the band. Shockwave numbs the site for 3-5 days, so 'it feels fine' is weak evidence this week. Run the written session, no extras. Tenderness to touch at the treated site is expected, pain that appears during running and worsens is not.
SELF-CARE: roll TFL, glutes and outer quad, never the band itself. No ice for 48h.
